body:
Follow-up hardening from T46 (PR #56). BLOCKED on upstream opencode support — check feasibility FIRST and close as won't-fix if the signal still does not exist.

ESTABLISHED DURING T46 (do not re-litigate)
- opencode does NOT fail closed when `--agent` cannot be honored: it warns and continues under the user's default primary agent, which typically permits write and bash.
- Under `--format default` that warning appears on stderr. Under `--format json` — which the review requires, because the default formatter interleaves tool framing into stdout and corrupts the payload — stderr is EMPTY and the fallback is completely silent. Verified: passing `--agent plan` (a subagent) produced no warning on any stream.
- Because there is no post-run signal, verification was moved to a PREFLIGHT: `opencode agent list` prints `<name> (primary|subagent)` computed from the same merged config the run will use, and the diff is not sent unless our agent is primary. Verified to report `(subagent)` when a project-local config downgrades the mode.

THE RESIDUAL
The preflight proves the merged config REGISTERS the agent as primary. It does not prove `run --agent <name>` HONORED it. Any divergence between list-time and run-time config loading, or a future opencode change that honors --agent at list time but not at run time, fails open with a clean exit and a normal-looking verdict. This was raised in three separate review passes and is the last known gap in the T46 sandbox.

GOAL
A signal the run itself emits that could not be produced by a fallback to the user's default agent, checked before the result is trusted.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC1  Establish whether opencode's `--format json` event stream exposes the active agent (session metadata, a step field, or an agent id on any event). Inspect a real stream. If it does not, close this ticket as blocked-upstream and record what was checked — do NOT invent a proxy signal that a fallback could also produce.
AC2  If a signal exists: after a run, require it to name the per-run agent, and refuse the result otherwise. The refusal must state that the review may have run unsandboxed. Verified in test/llm.test.js.
AC3  A PATH-gated test asserts the signal is present in a real sandboxed run and names the generated agent.
AC4  The check is verified to FAIL when the signal is absent — a test that cannot fail is not a control. Assert against a captured stream with the identity removed.
AC5  The existing preflight is retained, not replaced: it is what stops the diff being sent at all, and this attestation only guards the result afterwards.
AC6  npm test passes.

VERIFICATION COMMAND
npm test
title: Add an in-band attestation that the opencode sandbox agent actually ran
